home.title: Status

home.adminUnreachable: · Status API unreachable (if several frpc instances run on this machine, check whether port {port} is taken)
home.noProfile: No profile yet: create one under Profiles, or import an existing frpc.toml

home.hintIdle: Start frpc to see CPU / memory / uptime and the number of online proxies

home.hintLog: Status API is off: proxy and visitor status are inferred from logs, so real remote ports may be unavailable
home.noRules: This profile has no proxy rules yet — add some under Profiles

home.reloadRestarted: The admin API did not apply the new config, so the engine was restarted

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.noData: No data yet: start frpc with the status API enabled to see live status here

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoStart: Start the default profile when the app launches
settings.closeToTray: Minimize to tray when closing the window
settings.closeToTraySupport: frpc keeps running; reopen the window or quit from the tray icon
settings.accessLogsSupport: The status page refresh logs two lines every 4 seconds, hidden by default
settings.androidDataHint: Android cannot launch a system file manager; data lives in the app's private directory
settings.androidEngineOnly: Android always uses the bundled engine (libfrpc.so); custom paths are not supported.
settings.keepAliveHint: While a tunnel is running a persistent notification keeps the app in the foreground state, so the system does not reclaim the process (and kill the tunnel) when you switch away.
settings.keepAliveBatteryHint: Some OEM ROMs (Xiaomi / Huawei / OPPO…) also need background activity allowed, otherwise their battery saver may still kill the process.
settings.keepAliveRequested: System settings opened — choose "Don't restrict" or "Allow background activity"
settings.aboutTagline: Multi-profile GUI for frp: manage several tunnels at once, engine bundled in the app.
settings.aboutCopyFailed: Copy failed, please select the text manually

profiles.title: Server profiles
profiles.subtitle: Each profile targets one frps; imported frpc.toml files are cleaned up per proxy type
profiles.emptyHint: Click "New profile" to fill one in, or "Import" an existing frpc.toml
profiles.pendingHint: Saved but not reloaded — the old config is still in use
profiles.runningHint: Running — reload the config after saving
profiles.clearAllBody: This deletes {n} profiles (including proxy and visitor rules) and stops the running service. It cannot be undone — consider "Export all" first.
profiles.deleteBody: Delete "{name}" ({server}, {n} proxies)? This cannot be undone.
profiles.runningElsewhere: "{current}" is running — stop it before starting "{name}"
profiles.runningCannotDelete: "{name}" is running — stop it before deleting

editor.runningBody: You can edit and save, but frpc still uses the old config until you reload it (or stop and start again).
editor.name: Profile name
editor.nameSupport: Only distinguishes profiles on this machine; never written to frpc.toml
editor.serverAddrSupport: frps hostname or IP, without the http:// prefix
editor.serverPortSupport: bind_port for tcp/websocket; kcp_bind_port / quic_bind_port for kcp/quic
editor.clientIDSupport: Used by the frps dashboard to tell devices apart; empty = generated by frpc
editor.loginFailExit: Exit when the first login fails
editor.loginFailExitSupport: Off (default) = keep retrying, good for mobile networks; on = exit if the first attempt fails
editor.stunSupport: Only used for xtcp hole punching; the default is often unreachable in China — pick one that works
editor.authTokenSupport: Must match frps auth.token exactly (watch leading/trailing spaces)
editor.authNoneHint: Choose "No auth" when frps has no auth.token; a server that requires a token will reject this.
editor.metadatasTokenSupport: Only needed when frps enables the multiuser plugin; leave empty otherwise
editor.authUnsupported: This profile uses auth method "{method}", which the app cannot edit. Export frpc.toml and set it back to token or none, otherwise frpc fails to start due to missing oidc parameters.
editor.wsEnableSupport: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only; the app reads real remote ports and online state from it
editor.wsPortSupport: Use a different port for each profile running on the same machine
editor.wsPasswordSupport: Required when opening the status page in a browser
editor.tlsEnableSupport: On by default since frp v0.50; turn it off only if frps has TLS disabled
editor.poolCountSupport: Connections pre-established with frps to lower first-access latency; frp default is 1
editor.advancedShow: Advanced connection options (heartbeat / keepalive / bind address)
editor.heartbeatTimeoutSupport: Connection is considered dead after this long without a heartbeat
editor.muxKeepaliveSupport: Only effective when tcpMux is on
editor.connectServerLocalIP: Local source IP for connecting to frps (optional)
editor.connectServerLocalIPSupport: Pick the source address on multi-NIC / multi-egress hosts; empty = chosen by the system
editor.proxyURLSupport: Only effective when protocol = tcp. The app clears the system HTTP_PROXY, so use this field for an upstream proxy
editor.trustedCaFileSupport: Set the CA when frps uses a self-signed certificate, otherwise verification fails
editor.customTlsFirstByteSupport: Maps to disableCustomTLSFirstByte. Not sent by default; enable only for old frps versions
editor.customTransportSupport: When off, the transport section is not written and frpc defaults apply
editor.logToPlaceholder: empty = console only, collected by the app
editor.logToSupport: A file is written only when a path is set; the Logs page always shows console output live
editor.logMaxDaysSupport: Only affects logs written to a file
editor.disablePrintColorSupport: The app colors logs itself, so this removes a lot of ANSI escapes
editor.logConsoleHint: Logs always go to the console and are shown live on the Logs page (switch to debug when troubleshooting).
editor.proxiesSupport: Expose a local service through frps: tcp/udp by port, http/https/tcpmux by domain
editor.noProxies: No proxy rules yet: click "Add proxy" above, or import an existing frpc.toml under Profiles
editor.visitorsSupport: Reverse use: connect to someone else's stcp/sudp/xtcp private proxy and expose a local port for local apps
editor.saveRunningBody: After saving, frpc still uses the old config. Reload now to apply it?

proxyDialog.name: Proxy name
proxyDialog.remotePort: Remote port (empty = random; batch: 6001-6003, 8080,8081 create one rule per "name-port")

err.duplicateProxy: Proxy name "{name}" is already used by another rule
err.duplicateVisitor: Visitor name "{name}" is already used by another visitor

port.tooMany: "{token}" expands to more than {max} ports at once

reason.PORT_IN_USE: {label} is already in use, pick another port
reason.DUPLICATE_NAME: Proxy name "{name}" is duplicated; it must be unique on frps
reason.TYPE_FIELD_MISSING: A required field for this type is missing
reason.DOMAIN_OR_SUBDOMAIN_REQUIRED: A custom domain or subdomain is required (frp needs at least one)
reason.UNSUPPORTED_VALUE: {label} is not supported yet; export frpc.toml and set it manually
reason.FIELD_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_TYPE: {label} does not apply to this type (frp decodes strictly, so it would fail to start)
reason.BIND_PORT_REQUIRED: The local listen port cannot be 0 (frp reports "bind port is required"); use -1 to disable listening
reason.SUBDOMAIN_INVALID: A subdomain cannot contain . or * (use a custom domain for wildcards)
reason.BANDWIDTH_LIMIT_INVALID: Bandwidth limit needs a KB or MB unit, e.g. 1MB
reason.FALLBACK_VISITOR_NOT_FOUND: The fallback visitor does not exist, so there is no fallback when hole punching fails
reason.SERVER_NAME_PREFIX_DOUBLED: {label} should be the proxy name only. The prefix comes from "Remote device prefix"; empty means the local prefix
reason.XTCP_STUN_SERVER_NOT_SET: xtcp is used without a STUN server: frpc falls back to stun.easyvoip.com:3478, which often times out and breaks hole punching (visitors report "context deadline exceeded"). Configure a reachable one, e.g. stun.miwifi.com:3478

hint.XTCP_SERVER_MISSING: frps has no xtcp proxy named "{name}": check the visitor's "Remote proxy name"; for cross-device access, "Remote device prefix (serverUser)" must be the other side's user (not your own)
hint.PROXY_MISSING: frps has no proxy named "{name}": check the remote proxy name and the other side's user prefix
hint.STUN_TIMEOUT: The STUN server did not respond: configure a reachable STUN (e.g. stun.miwifi.com:3478) and retry; the other side must reach STUN too
hint.NOT_ENOUGH_ADDRESSES: STUN returned only one address, so the NAT type cannot be determined: use a public STUN with two addresses or run your own coturn
hint.NAT_HOLE_EXCHANGE_INFO: Hole punching timed out: the peer did not answer in time, usually because its frpc is not running, the keys differ, or its STUN is unreachable
hint.NAT_HOLE_PRECHECK_EOF: The control connection was closed by the server (frpc is reconnecting); if this repeats, check the network or whether frps restarted
hint.OPEN_TUNNEL_TIMEOUT: Hole punching did not succeed (timeout): common when both sides are behind symmetric NAT or cellular networks; configure "Fall back to" on the visitor to relay via frps
hint.XTCP_LISTENER_CLOSED: The local xtcp listener was closed: usually cleanup after the hole punching above failed or the app stopped; no action needed
hint.TOKEN_MISMATCH: The token does not match the server's auth.token: check the token in the config (watch leading/trailing spaces)
hint.LOGIN_IO_TIMEOUT: Cannot reach frps: check the server address/port and firewall, and whether a system proxy is intercepting the connection
